facts.quote: was born in Newark, October 17, 1822, the family then residing where Kuster's restaurant now stands.

facts.value: Subject of a biographical sketch in the Centennial History of the City of Newark and Licking County, Ohio (E. M. P. Brister; the scanned title page reads 1908).
facts.quote: he was the subject of a biographical sketch in 1909, which was published in the "1909 Centennial History of Newark and Licking County, Ohio'.

facts.value: Attended the Newark public schools until age twelve.
facts.quote: The boyhood days of Stephen A. Gill were spent in Newark, where he attended the public schools until he reached the age of twelve years

facts.value: At twelve he moved with his parents to a 184-acre farm in Union township.
facts.quote: removed with his parents to a farm of one hundred and eighty-four acres in Union township.

facts.value: Farmer specialising in sheep breeding and wool growing until 1906.
facts.quote: He engaged in general agricultural pursuits making a specialty of sheep breeding and wool growing, until the year 1906

facts.value: Retired to Hebron in 1906.
facts.quote: when he removed to Hebron, where he is now living in retirement

facts.value: Married Miss Harriet J. Adams.
facts.quote: On March 8, 1848, he wedded Miss Harriet J. Adams

facts.value: Voted Republican in national and state politics.
facts.quote: In his political views Mr. Gill is a republican

facts.value: Faithful member of the Licking Baptist church, where he had been a deacon for the previous five years.
facts.quote: a faithful adherent of the Licking Baptist church, of which he has for the past five years been a deacon.

facts.value: In the 1850 census his household included an Elizabeth Adams, age 67.
facts.quote: living with the Stephen Gill family in Union Township, Licking County, Ohio.

facts.value: A girl named Mary Swan was living with the Gills in the 1860 census.
facts.quote: Also, notice the girl residing with the Gills, Mary Swan.

facts.value: Mary R. Adams was listed as his niece in his household in the 1880 census.
facts.quote: Mary R. Adams turns up in the 1880 census, where else but in the Stephen Gill family, and is listed as a niece!

facts.value: A Ralph S. Adams was living in the Gill household in the 1900 census.
facts.quote: there is a Ralph S. Adams living in the Gill household as well.

facts.value: Head of household in the 1870 census
facts.quote: US Census 1870, Etna Township, Licking County, Ohio, Stephen A. Gill household

facts.place: Cedar Hill Cemetery, Newark, Licking County, Ohio
facts.value: Buried with Harriet Josephine at Cedar Hill Cemetery
facts.quote: phen & Harriet Josephine (Adams) Gill Cedar Hill Cemetery

facts.value: Harriet Ray Adams was the informant on his death certificate
facts.quote: Harriet Adams who was the informant for Stephen Gill’s death certificate.

facts.value: Described in 1889 as an old and prominent citizen of Union Township
facts.quote: an old and prominent citizen of Union township.

facts.value: Born in Saxony (Germany) per the 1860 census.
facts.quote: a wife, Christiana, born in Saxony (Germany)

facts.value: Married A. W. Adams.
facts.quote: Kw W Adams & c F Konitzer Marriage Record, May 26, 1851, Franklin County, Ohio

facts.value: 1840 census household headed by Lewis Swan(n), three members: male 10-14, male 30-39, female 20-29
facts.quote: enumerates a household headed by Lewis Swan(n) in Union Township, Licking County, Ohio, with three family members

facts.value: 1850 census household: Lewis 43, Mary E. 33, Horatio M. 23, Melissa 18, Mary Elizabeth 10
facts.quote: Lewis, age 43; Mary E., age 33; Horatio M., age 23; Melissa, age 18 and Mary Elizabeth, age 10.

facts.value: Spent the rest of his life moving between his children's households and the Gills'
facts.quote: Lewis spends the rest of his life bouncing around between his children’s and the Gills households.

facts.value: Died about 1802 in Jefferson Co., VA
facts.quote: d. c1802, Jefferson Co., VA

facts.place: Shepherdstown area, along the Potomac River
facts.value: Lived near Shepherdstown; his land lay along the Potomac River
facts.quote: Francis lived in the area of Shepherdstown, his land situated along the Potomac River.

facts.place: Keeptrist, Berkeley Co., VA (now Jefferson Co., WV)
facts.value: Settled at Keeptrist in 1773 and was still there on 19 May 1784; Keeptrist was formerly John Semple's property, site of Keeptrist Furnace on Elk Run
facts.quote: He lived at Keeptrist, in Berkeley Co., VA (now Jefferson Co., WV) where he settled in 1773, and was there on 19 May 1784.

facts.value: His brother Alexander fled from Prince George's County to Keeptrist in 1777.
facts.quote: It was here that his brother Alexander fled from Prince George's county in 1777.

facts.value: Left a will, but it was recorded in a lost book of Berkeley Co.; heirs are named in the court suit North vs. the heirs of Francis HAMILTON, in brother Alexander's will, and in grandson Francis Alexander HAMILTON's will
facts.quote: He left a will, but unfortunately it was recorded in one of the lost books of Berkeley Co., VA.

facts.value: Witnessed a lease from Joseph McCormick Mason to John Semple for 400 acres; must have been in America by 1765
facts.quote: On 31 May 1765, he witnessed a lease between Joseph McCormick Mason of PA, to John Semple

facts.value: Appointed with Thomas Hart, Henry Lloyd and Godwin Smith to view ground for a road from Semples Furnace to the Warm Springs Road
facts.quote: On 4 Apr 1769 Thomas Hart, Henry Lloyd, Godwin Smith, and Francis were appointed to view ground from Semples Furnace to the Warm Springs Road

facts.value: Bought from John Keys for 35 pounds a bay horse, a feather bed and furniture, and a share in a 1769 tobacco crop
facts.quote: On 30 Apr 1771 John Keys sold to Francis for 35 pounds, one bay horse, one feather Bed and furniture

facts.value: John Semple, indebted to him, conveyed cows, furniture and grain to him
facts.quote: 1 Jun 1773, John Semple was indebted to Francis HAMLTON conveyed cows, furniture, and grain to said HAMILTON

facts.value: Slave owner, taxed in 1774 for slaves Peter, Roger, Sarah, Beck, Jeremiah and Thomas
facts.quote: As a slave owner, he was taxed in 1774 for slaves Peter, Roger, Sarah, Beck, Jeremiah, and Thomas.

facts.value: Listed at the sale of Abraham Buckle's estate
facts.quote: On 28 Jun 1777 he was listed at a sale of Abraham Buckle's estate.

facts.value: Witnessed the will of Barbara Merriotes (Merritt?)
facts.quote: He witnessed the will of Barbara Merriotes (Merritt?) on 20 Dec 1778.

facts.value: Bought Lot 42 in Sharpsburg from Michael Taylor for 2 pounds
facts.quote: On 13 Sep 1779, Michael Taylor of Washington Co., MD sold to Francis HAMILTON for 2 pounds, Lot 42 in Sharpsburg

facts.value: One of the executors of the will of Andrew Telleroy
facts.quote: He was one of the executors to the will of Andrew Telleroy on 22 Noy 1780.

facts.value: In 1782-1787 paid tax on 1 poll and 5 slaves in Berkeley Co.; named in audits of John Creighton's (19 Mar 1782) and Robert T. Tabb's (20 Aug 1782) estates and attended the sale of Barbara Merritt's estate
facts.quote: In the years spanning 1782-1787 he paid tax on 1 pole, 5 slaves in Berkeley Co.

facts.value: David Meek's will left 10 pounds to Francis HAMILTON of Berkeley Co.
facts.quote: On_23 Mar 1783, David Meek in his will in Frederick Co., MD, left 10 pounds to Francis HAMILTON of Berkeley Co.

facts.value: Taxed on 4 white males 16-21, 7 blacks above 16, 12 blacks under 16 and 13 horses in the district of Commissioner Thomas Hart; neighbors included David Evans, the Hagelys, the Houtes, Henry Jacob, John Moler, Elizabeth Rianer and John Womandorf
facts.quote: On 20 Jun 1786 Francis was taxed on 4 white males 16 and under 21, 7 blacks above 16, 12 blacks under 16, and 13 horses

facts.value: Named in the settlement of George Adam MOLER's estate, and in the 2nd settlement on 21 Jan 1793
facts.quote: On 20 Apr 1789 he was named in the settlement of George Adam OLER'S (MOLER) estate.

facts.value: Bought 123 acres in Berkeley Co. from Henry Lee of Stafford Co., VA
facts.quote: In 1790 he bought 123a in Berkeley Co., from Henry Lee of Stafford Co., VA.

facts.value: Witnessed the will of Isaac Strider
facts.quote: He witnessed the will of Isaac Strider on 10 Jun_1793.

facts.value: Bought 120 acres from Peter Fleck, previously owned by Charles Friend
facts.quote: on 17 Dec 1796 he bought land from Peter Fleck in Berkeley Co., 120 acres previously owned by Charles Friend.

facts.value: Three estate records exist in Jefferson Co. (pages missing); property distributed to heirs on 20 Apr 1809
facts.quote: On 20 Apr 1809, the property was distributed to the heirs: John 47 acres, Jacobina 47 acres, Walter BAKER (m. Magdalena) 39 1/2 acres

facts.value: No burial site has been found
facts.quote: No burial site has been found, and no marriage for Francis.

facts.value: He and his wife (Gavin's parents) were rebuked by the Kirk Session before their marriage for 'unseasonable fruitfulness', that is, a pregnancy before marriage.
facts.quote: up to his reputation of having a heart of gold. He rejoiced in liberal views. His father and mother had been obliged
